title: PolicyQuery
description: One question to the policy worker (ADR-010 §2): the player's own observation, the candidate joint choices of that request and how to pick among them. It carries no seed, no verdict on a pending candidate and nothing of the opponent's. The answer is a PolicyReply holding a Recommendation. identity equals observation.identity: a reader rule (the profile cannot compare two fields), checked by the worker.

query_id.description: Correlates a reply with its query on one worker session: assigned by the client, unique among the queries outstanding, echoed in the reply. Not part of what the encoder reads.

identity.description: The request this query asks to answer; equal to observation.identity (a reader rule).

observation.description: Built by the ObservationBuilder from the Episode's own channel prefix.

candidates.description: The candidate joint choices of the request, each with its pending flag, in the enumerator's canonical order (ADR-006); the choice is one of them. The same N_max as TrainingExample.candidates (ADR-010 §3). No CloneJudge verdict is ever part of it.

candidate_features.description: Optional derived candidate features (ADR-022 section 3, tier A): the probe's damage rows for the damaging move parts of the candidates, computed on the Node side from the player's own channel, own team, the candidates and the configs feature_set_hash names. Absent unless the session or the run declared a feature set: a writer omits it (never null or empty), so every existing value keeps its bytes and hash (a minor change within v1, ADR-008 section 3). Reader rules: rows sorted and unique by (slot, move, target, mega); and, in a PolicyQuery, every damaging move part of every candidate has its row (the worker answers invalid_query otherwise) and feature_set_hash equals the one the session declared.

sampling.description: How the worker picks among the candidates (ADR-010 §2): argmax, a draw from the policy's probabilities using u, or (ADR-026 §5) no pick at all: evaluate asks for the policy's prior over the candidates and its value of the state.

policy_id.description: The inference identity that produced the choice (ADR-010 §2): echoed as the Recommendation's source_policy_id.

PreviewObservation.description: What one player may know at a Team Preview decision (ADR-008 §5): their own channel, request and team. Built only by the ObservationBuilder.

data_class.description: private when the team or the channel it was built from is private.

identity.description: The request this observation asks to answer.

log.description: This player's channel up to and including that |request| line, as the engine split it (ADR-008 §5): never the omniscient log.

decision_context.description: Timer and budget; excluded by name from A1/A2 equality (ADR-008 §4).

BattleObservation.description: What one player may know at a move or forced-switch decision (ADR-008 §5): their own channel, request and team. Built only by the ObservationBuilder.

data_class.description: private when the team or the channel it was built from is private.

identity.description: The request this observation asks to answer.

log.description: This player's channel up to and including that |request| line, as the engine split it (ADR-008 §5): never the omniscient log.

decision_context.description: Timer and budget; excluded by name from A1/A2 equality (ADR-008 §4).

VersionManifest.description: Replay identity of a battle (ADR-003, ADR-007): the pinned engine commit, the format, and the hashes of the engine ruleset and of Areneon's own format rules.

ruleset_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical engine ruleset.

format_rules_hash.description: SHA-256 of Areneon's format rules record (ADR-007).

RequestIdentity.description: Which request a decision answers (ADR-008 §4). A consumer drops a recommendation unless request_seq and request_hash both match, and rqid too when both carry one.

request_seq.description: Areneon's 1-based count of the requests one player has received in this battle, including wait requests.

request_hash.description: SHA-256 of the canonical request JSON without rqid (ADR-008 §4): lowercase hex.

rqid.description: The Showdown server's request id; present only on the server path (A2), never hashed.

PrivateTeamSpec.description: A player's or the bot's own full team. Never part of another player's observation; a private one is never committed.

data_class.description: synthetic: CC0, may be committed; private: a real team or a human's games, kept only in private-data/ (ADR-008 §5).

PokemonSet.description: One set, as the pinned engine's PokemonSet (sim/teams.ts) holds it. Legality is the engine validator's, not this schema's.

evs.description: Stat Points in the champions mod (ADR-003).

DecisionContext.description: Timer state and deadline budget for one decision (#678 §4.2). Relative durations only, never wall-clock time. Excluded by name from A1/A2 observation equality (ADR-008 §4).

timer_source.description: server: the server's own timer snapshot; shadow: Areneon's model of it (#678 §2.1).

turn_seconds_left.description: T: seconds left this turn at receipt.

bank_seconds_left.description: B: bank seconds left at receipt, grace excluded.

grace_seconds_left.description: G: grace seconds left at receipt; non-zero only at Team Preview.

remaining_decisions_estimate.description: R̂: estimated decisions left; battle only, omitted at Team Preview.

submit_within_ms.description: The choice must be sent within this, from receipt.

policy_budget_ms.description: The policy must answer within this; 0 means skip the policy and send the fallback.

TimerRules.description: The format's VGC Timer settings in whole seconds; they must equal the version manifest's.

grace.description: Grace time, spent only at Team Preview.

add_per_turn.description: Seconds added to the bank per turn.

max_first_turn.description: Cap on the first turn's time.

CandidateFeatures.description: The rows of one decision under one feature set. feature_set names the set (probe-damage/1 or probe-damage/2); feature_set_hash is SHA-256 of the JCS of its identity (mechanics config, assumed-set config, adapter format, reader, version manifest), so a pin bump or a config change is another set. Rows are in canonical order: slot, move, target, then mega false before true. Under probe-damage/2 the four arrays threats, speeds, own_priorities and foe_priorities are all present; under any other set none is (a reader rule: the profile has no if/then).

rows.description: One row per distinct (slot, move, target, mega) that some candidate uses with a damaging move into an opposing active; empty when the request has none (Team Preview, a forced switch).

threats.description: probe-damage/2 only: one row per (own Pokemon and variant, opposing active, revealed damaging move of that foe), sorted by (own, mega false first, foe, move id). Values on the assumed opponent set, not facts about the real opponent.

speeds.description: probe-damage/2 only: exactly one row per (own position, own Mega flag, foe location), for every own active and every switch-in a candidate names, sorted by (own, mega false first, foe).

own_priorities.description: probe-damage/2 only: one row per own move part of the candidates, sorted by (slot, move, mega false first).

foe_priorities.description: probe-damage/2 only: one row per revealed move of each opposing active, sorted by (foe, move id).

ComputedFeatureRow.description: The probe's exact rolls for one row, as integers: mean_ppm is the mean over the 16 no-crit rolls of min(roll, hp) / hp, floored; max_ppm and min_ppm the largest and smallest roll clamped at hp, as a share of hp; ohko_rolls the probe's own count of the 16 no-crit rolls that reach hp, or null when the probe gives none.

move.description: The move's position in the request, 1-based.

target.description: The opposing target's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

mega.description: True when the move part also Mega Evolves.

UnsupportedFeatureRow.description: A row the probe could not answer exactly: its closed reason (the MechanicsResult unsupported reasons), never a guess.

Candidate.description: One candidate joint choice (ADR-006): canonical engine syntax and whether its legality depends on information the engine hides from the player.

choice.description: Canonical engine syntax, e.g. move 1 2 mega, switch 3.

pending.description: True when the legality of the choice depends on hidden information (maybeTrapped, maybeDisabled, maybeLocked); no verdict on it is ever given.

ArgmaxSampling.description: The first candidate with the highest probability.

SampleSampling.description: The first candidate, in order, whose cumulative probability exceeds u / 2^53 (the probabilities summed in float64; at temperature 1 and without a truncation unless the optional fields below say otherwise).

u.description: The first 53 bits of SHA-256(JCS({seed, game, player, policy_id, request_seq})), computed by the client: the worker never receives the seed.

temperature_ppm.description: Play temperature in millionths (ADR-023 §1): the probabilities are softmax(logits * 10^6 / temperature_ppm) over the real candidates, in float32. Absent means 1,000,000 (temperature 1). Writers omit it at the default: a reader rule refuses an explicit 1,000,000, so one rule has one encoding.

truncation.description: An optional play-time truncation of the probabilities before the draw (ADR-023 §1). Absent means none.

EvaluateSampling.description: No candidate is chosen: the worker answers with an EvaluationReply (not a PolicyReply recommendation) holding the policy's probability of each candidate (temperature 1, no truncation) and its value of the state, from one batch-1 forward pass. candidate_features are read as for any other query. The query is a decision-time search's question; policy_id names the policy asked.

ThresholdTruncation.description: Every candidate whose probability is below min_ppm / 10^6 gets probability 0, except that the first highest candidate is always kept; the rest are renormalised. Applied after the temperature, before the draw.

ComputedThreatRow.description: What the foe's revealed damaging move does to the own Pokemon (the foe's assumed set as attacker, the own Pokemon at its exact current HP): the values of a ComputedFeatureRow, as integers.

own.description: The own Pokemon's position in the request's side.pokemon, 0-based.

mega.description: True for the variant of the own Pokemon that Mega Evolves this turn.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

UnsupportedThreatRow.description: A threat the probe could not answer exactly: its closed reason, never a guess.

own.description: The own Pokemon's position in the request's side.pokemon, 0-based.

mega.description: True for the variant of the own Pokemon that Mega Evolves this turn.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

ComputedSpeedRow.description: Who acts first between the own Pokemon (and variant) and the opposing active, as the engine orders their action speed.

own.description: The own Pokemon's position in the request's side.pokemon, 0-based.

mega.description: True for the variant of the own Pokemon that Mega Evolves this turn.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

UnsupportedSpeedRow.description: A speed relation the probe could not answer: the probe's closed reasons, or unqueueable / fractional_priority.

own.description: The own Pokemon's position in the request's side.pokemon, 0-based.

mega.description: True for the variant of the own Pokemon that Mega Evolves this turn.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

ComputedOwnPriorityRow.description: The engine's priority key of one own move part of the candidates.

move.description: The move's position in the request, 1-based.

mega.description: True when the move part also Mega Evolves.

priority.description: The engine's priority key of the move, as the probe's ActionOrder.priority.

UnsupportedOwnPriorityRow.description: An own priority the probe could not answer: the probe's closed reasons, or unqueueable / fractional_priority (a pseudo-move such as recharge is query_kind).

ComputedFoePriorityRow.description: The engine's priority key of one revealed move of an opposing active.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).

priority.description: The engine's priority key of the move, as the probe's ActionOrder.priority.

UnsupportedFoePriorityRow.description: A foe priority the probe could not answer: the probe's closed reasons, or unqueueable / fractional_priority.

foe.description: The opposing active's location number in a choice (move 1 1).
